data.one_liner: Flutter plugin to handle Wi-Fi connections and hotspot (AP, STA) on Android and iOS
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter apps to manage Wi-Fi connections, view network status, connect/disconnect from Wi-Fi networks in WPA/WEP, and handle Access Point (AP) features on supported platforms. Provides functions for reading SSID, BSSID, IP, signal strength, and forcing Wi-Fi traffic routing.
use_when: You need to connect your Flutter app directly to specific Wi-Fi networks programmatically
You need to check current Wi-Fi connection info like SSID, BSSID, and IP address
You need to manage local-only hotspots or Wi-Fi access points on Android
avoid_when: You need robust, modern Wi-Fi network scanning (the scanning feature is discontinued; use wifi_scan instead)
You are building for iOS and require full control over Wi-Fi module enabling/disabling or advanced AP configurations (not supported on iOS)
You only need basic internet connectivity checks (use connectivity_plus instead)
strengths: Provides fine-grained control over Wi-Fi connections and network registration
Supports forcing traffic routing via connected access point (`forceWifiUsage`)
Cross-platform support for both Android and iOS with tailored capabilities
weaknesses: Many features have strong limitations, deprecations, or are completely unavailable on iOS due to Apple's platform restrictions
Android SDK updates (SDK >= 26 and >= 29) significantly restrict Wi-Fi AP and module management behaviors
Scanning functionality is discontinued in this package
data.setup_notes: Requires specifying `use_frameworks!` in your iOS Podfile. Certain Android functions require explicit permissions (like CHANGE_WIFI_STATE or WRITE_SETTINGS) depending on usage.
data.minimal_example: bool result = await WiFiForIoTPlugin.connect('SSID', password: 'PASSWORD', security: NetworkSecurity.WPA);
